📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the DC Council’s Committee on Human Services will mark up and vote on B26-0656 at 3 p.m.
  • The District’s online casino bill is moving again, with little time to spare.
  • Sources indicate that the calendar is tight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the DC Council’s Committee on Human Services will mark up and vote on B26-0656 at 3 p.m. on Nov. 18, the bill’s first movement since its only hearing on May 4. The bill would legalize online casinos and ban dual-currency sweepstakes casinos, and few legislative days remain this year.

The District’s online casino bill is moving again, with little time to spare.

Sources indicate that the calendar is tight. Council Period 26 closes at 11:59 a.m. on Jan. 2, 2027. Any permanent bill that has not received final reading by the Dec. 15 legislative meeting lapses at the end of the period and must start over in Council Period 27.

According to recent reports, the committee’s makeup may help. Its members include the bill’s sponsor, Wendell Felder, along with Christina Henderson and Zachary Parker. The committee also oversees the Office of Lottery and Gaming, which would regulate the upcoming market.

Felder remarked in his introduction letter that the bill is meant to authorize, regulate and tax internet gaming in the District. If it passes, DC would join the small group of jurisdictions with legal online casinos.

The bill would also ban dual-currency sweepstakes casinos, and it comes with enforcement tools. The Office of Lottery and Gaming could send cease-and-desist letters. The DC Attorney General could go to court and seize profits.

Launch would not be immediate. The introduced bill says internet gaming cannot start until the District’s chief financial officer certifies that the regulatory system is ready.

Sources indicate that the licensing terms favor operators already in the District. Suppliers would pay $50,000 to apply and $25,000 to renew. There is no cap on operator licenses, and each operator could run up to two skins.

Holders of a DC sports wagering operator license or another gaming license would get expedited review. The Office of Lottery and Gaming could rely on earlier background checks. BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, Fanatics and FanDuel all offer online sports betting in DC.

Industry support was visible at the May hearing. Caesars, DraftKings and BetMGM all backed the bill. Thomas R. Burnside, executive director of the Office of Lottery and Gaming, testified and attached proposed changes to the bill.

October was a big month for DC Lottery players! Over $9 million in total prizes were won across DC Lottery games this October. From scratch-off tickets to DC 5 and iLottery games, players had plenty of exciting wins to celebrate.

Congratulations… pic.twitter.com/1PszcyW9Uo.

— DC Lottery (@DCLottery) November 15, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the regulator also flagged a trade-off for its own business. Its director acknowledged that online casinos could eat into iLottery sales. He stated online casino revenue would offset any losses.

Any amendments adopted at markup will show whether Burnside’s proposed changes made it into the committee version. Once the committee has voted on Nov. 18, the full Council’s remaining legislative meetings fall on Dec. 1 and Dec. 15.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A woman in Germany was slapped with a €25 ($27 USD) fine after sitting down on a bench at a children’s playground to cry, unaware that she was breaking the law by being there without a child.
  • The 31-year-old woman, identified as Hana, had gone for a walk through Glückaufpark in Gelsenkirchen on October 25 to clear her head after becoming overwhelmed by financial and academic pressures.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A woman in Germany was slapped with a €25 ($27 USD) fine after sitting down on a bench at a children’s playground to cry, unaware that she was breaking the law by being there without a child.

The 31-year-old woman, identified as Hana, had gone for a walk through Glückaufpark in Gelsenkirchen on October 25 to clear her head after becoming overwhelmed by financial and academic pressures.

The chemistry student eventually broke down in tears, taking a seat on a bench at the playground and calling her aunt.

“I just wanted to be alone and not be seen by anyone,” she told German broadcaster WDR.

Industry observers note that however, three municipal enforcement officers approached her and asked whether two boys playing on the swings were her children. When she remarked no, the officers demanded her identification and issued her a €25 fine.

Under Gelsenkirchen’s municipal regulations, playgrounds are reserved for children aged 14 and under, along with their parents, guardians, and supervisors.

While there was a sign outlining the playground’s rules, BILD reports that it did not explicitly state that unaccompanied adults were prohibited from sitting on the benches.

Hana argued that the officers could have simply asked her to move instead of issuing a fine.

“I felt as though I was worth nothing as a human being,” she said.

Despite criticism, the city defended the officers’ actions, describing the fine as relatively mild and proportionate. According to WELT, Hana has since paid the fine to avoid incurring additional costs.

Rather than relaxing the rules, the city council discussed increasing the maximum penalty for playground violations from €55 to €60 ($66) on November 17.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Garmin and Bark are competing for your money this year, and these sales make it easy to get something fun that’ll keep your kids safe and in touch.
  • According to recent reports, many parents struggle with the idea of getting a smartphone for their kids.
  • Both watches are on sale well ahead of Black Friday, too!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Garmin and Bark are competing for your money this year, and these sales make it easy to get something fun that’ll keep your kids safe and in touch.

According to recent reports, many parents struggle with the idea of getting a smartphone for their kids. If you want your kids to stay in touch but not have access to all the garbage on the internet, a smartwatch is the best alternative. I’ve tested a lot of kids’ smartwatches over the years, and I can easily recommend the two in the picture above: the Bark Watch and the Garmin Bounce 2.

Both watches are on sale well ahead of Black Friday, too! The Bark Watch is $11 off at Amazon ($274 total) and $50 off at Bark, while the Garmin Bounce 2 is $50-$64 off (starting at $235) depending on the color you choose. The least expensive Garmin Bounce 2 is the blue color in the photo I took above, which my son loved.

Choosing between the two is easy enough. Garmin’s watch is the least complicated and comes in a slightly more durable case with fun colors. It’s slightly cheaper than Bark, but doesn’t have any health sensors on board. It mainly tracks steps, allows your kids to message or call you, and gives you geofencing and location tracking through a $9.99 per month LTE subscription blueprint. It’s got a 5ATM rating and a polycarbonate case, so it’s quite durable.

It has been revealed that the Garmin Bounce 2 is preloaded with a few mini games and educational apps, plus the Garmin Jr. app has built-in unlockables and rewards parents can set for doing chores, completing schoolwork, etc. Battery life is roughly 2 days with normal use, but can be less if you’re in an area with poor LTE reception. The Garmin Bounce 2 is best for kids 10 and under.

It has been revealed that the Bark Watch uses Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 hardware and a custom version of Wear OS. It’s a much more powerful watch and only gets a day of battery life because of it. This one feels like a midpoint between a kids’ watch and a standard Wear OS watch, as it has all the power of Wear OS but doesn’t feature the Google Play Store. It doesn’t have any games, social media, or browsers.

Since it uses Samsung’s hardware, it includes cutting-edge health sensors that your kids can use, plus great multitasking and a svelte, attractive design. Bark charges $15 per month for its strategy, which includes a Bark App subscription for the whole family. I also use the Bark App on my son’s phone, which helps me monitor his usage and make sure he’s safe online. The extra $5 per month adds up, but it’s absolutely worth it if you want to add the Bark App to another phone or tablet.

The Bark Watch is fine enough for younger kids, but the design and lack of games feel more like an “older kids’ watch” to me, and my 12-year-old son agrees. Either way you go, these are fantastic choices that you’ll be happy with, especially with a nice little deal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clicks is still on track to release the phone with a physical keyboard within the next few months, but a Communicator launch before the end of this year isn’t looking very likely as shipping gets pushed back.

The Communicator is a fresh take on what an Android phone can be. It was first introduced at CES earlier this year, with the main selling angle being the physically integrated keyboard. Clicks wants to target those who are looking for a second device, and the Communicator fits the bill.

In a recent development, last we heard, the Clicks Communicator was on track to launch and ship in December, following a cheery upgrade detailing an upgrade to 12GB of RAM and other changes. However, Clicks posted a latest update today stating that the timeline has shifted out a month because of supply chain challenges caused by something other than RAM.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, we’ve encountered a delay with securing a critical supply chain component needed to fabricate our printed circuit board ahead of manufacturing and final assembly. Assembly will now begin in early January, with deliveries expected to start in late January.

It notes that the “critical supply chain component” is the essential fabric used for the tech giant’s printed circuit boards. The blog post dives into some neat details about the component holding things up. The PCBs Clicks is using are made up of more material layers than some competitor boards. But the fabric used to layer those boards is in short supply at this sort of demand, with four manufacturers reportedly unable to meet the company’s required volume.

Recent findings suggest that the post also spells out difficulties caused by troubles in the Middle East, and rising memory costs straining the chain of supply further, even if memory – surprisingly – isn’t the cause of this small delay. Those compounded problems have pushed production back, and owners are now told to expect their Clicks Communicator pre-orders to be shipped in late January, at the earliest. Many pre-orders will likely be shipped after that because of further time constraints before Chinese New Year.

In an act of good faith, Clicks says it’s including a set of 3.5mm wired headphones in each box for orders placed prior to today.

Sources indicate that A push from December to January isn’t massive, and Clicks still seems to be making solid time on developing a form factor we don’t often see. You can still pre-order the Clicks Communicator starting at $649.

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (985 w)

Latest Update: The ultimate monitor for CS2 and Valorant: What actually matters?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In competitive shooters like Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, and Call of Duty, every millisecond counts.
  • In a recent development, but while graphics cards usually get most of the attention, your monitor plays a huge role in how smooth and responsive a game feels.
  • With gaming monitors now hitting 480Hz and beyond, refresh rates are reaching some pretty astonishing numbers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In competitive shooters like Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, and Call of Duty, every millisecond counts. Players are constantly looking for ways to get an edge, whether that’s upgrading their PC, tweaking settings, or investing in a faster monitor.

In a recent development, but while graphics cards usually get most of the attention, your monitor plays a huge role in how smooth and responsive a game feels. After all, there’s only so much benefit to pushing hundreds of frames per second if your display can’t keep up.

With gaming monitors now hitting 480Hz and beyond, refresh rates are reaching some pretty astonishing numbers. But you might be asking, can you actually feel the difference, and is upgrading from 144Hz or 240Hz really worth it?

In competitive shooters, where quick reactions and precise aiming matter, a monitor’s refresh rate can influence how smoothly movement appears on screen.

According to recent reports, A higher refresh rate allows the display to update its image more frequently. For example, a 144Hz monitor refreshes approximately every 6.94 milliseconds, while a 480Hz display refreshes every 2.08 milliseconds.

That difference can help players track moving opponents and receive updated visual information sooner, particularly in fast-paced games like Counter-Strike 2 and Valorant.

However, the benefits become smaller at higher refresh rates, and players need a PC capable of producing enough frames to take full advantage of them.

Industry observers note that refresh rate isn’t the only factor affecting motion clarity, either. OLED panels generally offer much faster pixel response times than traditional LCD monitors, reducing the ghosting that can appear behind moving objects.

Why you should upgrade to an OLED for GTA 6.

The best gaming monitor in 2024: Budget, 4K & Ultrawide.

The best refresh rate for Counter-Strike 2.

GIGABYTE’s AORUS ELITE lineup combines those fast response times with high refresh rates, offering different options depending on how players use their monitors.

The AORUS FO32U24G features a 32-inch fourth-generation Tandem WOLED panel with a 0.03ms GTG response time. Its Dual Mode technology allows players to switch between two display configurations:.

It has been revealed that this approach could appeal to players who regularly switch between different genres. Someone playing Counter-Strike 2 might prefer the 480Hz mode, while a player enjoying a visually demanding single-player game could switch back to 4K.

The smaller AORUS FO27Q28G takes a different approach, offering a 27-inch QHD Tandem WOLED panel with a 280Hz refresh rate and the same advertised 0.03ms GTG response time.

Both monitors also support NVIDIA G-SYNC compatibility and AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, which can help reduce tearing when frame rates fluctuate.

Refresh rate and response time aren’t the only specifications to focus on.

Modern gaming monitors increasingly include built-in features designed to give players more control over visibility, screen layout, and the information displayed during gameplay.

GIGABYTE’s AORUS ELITE monitors include several Tactical Features intended for different competitive scenarios:.

Some of these features may be particularly relevant to Counter-Strike 2 players, many of whom have specific preferences for screen size, resolution, and aspect ratio.

Tactical Switch 2.0 allows players to change between different display configurations without manually adjusting every setting, while Tactical HUD could be useful in games where players regularly need to reference mini-maps or other on-screen information.

GIGABYTE also includes Night Vision and AI Black Equalizer to improve visibility in darker environments, alongside Ultra Clear, which uses black-frame insertion to reduce perceived motion blur.

Recent findings suggest that not every feature will be useful to every player, and some display-side assists may be restricted under competitive tournament rules. Players should check the rules of the games and competitions they participate in before using them.

Although 480Hz monitors offer extremely frequent display updates, not every competitive player needs the highest available refresh rate.

For someone upgrading from a 60Hz or 75Hz display, even moving to 144Hz can make a substantial difference in perceived smoothness.

Players already using 240Hz or 280Hz monitors may notice a smaller improvement when switching to 480Hz, particularly if their PC struggles to maintain the frame rates required to take advantage of it.

Recent findings suggest that A 480Hz monitor makes the most sense for players who prioritize competitive performance and have a PC capable of producing extremely high frame rates. For others, a 280Hz OLED may provide a better balance between responsiveness, resolution, and everyday use.

GIGABYTE’s M series offers several alternatives depending on panel technology, screen finish, and gaming preferences:.

The MO27Q2A provides a QD-OLED alternative for players who want fast response times and high refresh rates, while the MO27Q28G and MO27Q28GR offer different screen finishes depending on the environment.

The M27UP takes a different approach with an IPS panel, making it an option for players who want 4K gaming and high-refresh competitive performance without moving to OLED.

For players considering OLED, long-term panel care is another factor worth keeping in mind.

Competitive shooters frequently display static interface elements, including health bars, ammunition counters, mini-maps, and scoreboards. Over extended periods, these elements can contribute to uneven pixel wear.

GIGABYTE’s AORUS ELITE FO32U24G and FO27Q28G feature AI OLED Care Pro, which includes automated pixel cleaning, brightness adjustments, and display protection designed to reduce burn-in risk.

The MO27Q2A, MO27Q28G, and MO27Q28GR instead feature AI OLED Care, providing background panel maintenance and protection.

While 480Hz OLED monitors represent a high-performance option for competitive gaming, they aren’t necessarily the right choice for everyone.

Players who spend most of their time in Counter-Strike 2 or Valorant and have PCs capable of producing hundreds of frames per second may benefit from the additional responsiveness.

For those who split their time between competitive shooters and visually demanding single-player games, a lower-refresh OLED with higher resolution may make more sense.

Ultimately, the best gaming monitor isn’t always the one with the highest refresh rate. It’s the one that matches the games you play, the hardware you own, and the experience you’re trying to achieve.

Following the Android deprecation in September, Google Assistant is going away on speakers and smart displays next year. Additionally, Google Home is fully replacing the Nest app in January.

In a recent development, the Nest app on Android, iOS, and the web will stop working on January 25, 2027. The Google Home app, which requires a Google Account, will be needed to “continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely.”.

Officially, Google wants to “focus all of [its] engineering, security, and feature investments on one unified, modern experience.” It reiterated benefits like:.

It has been revealed that with home.nest.com going away, you have to download any custom video clips since they will not transfer over to Google Home. A one-click “Download All” button is available.

Industry observers note that terrible news. For all my first-gen Nest cameras (wired hello doorbell, wired outdoor cams, and multiple indoor cams), I vastly prefer the Nest app to the terrible Google Home app.

Industry observers note that otherwise, Nest app users do not need to do anything else, with devices automatically transferring over to the Google Home app. No Nest thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke alarms, or locks are losing support with this change.

Additionally, Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions will automatically switch to Google Home Premium “with no additional cost and no credit card re-entry required at this time.”.

Industry observers note that the other change announced today is that Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays is going away on August 2, 2027. It will be replaced by the Gemini for Home voice assistant. Google notes that natural language support replaces “rigid, static and highly specific voice commands.” Additionally:.

Sources indicate that you can upgrade to Gemini today, while Google is expanding international availability over the coming months. Google will share more updates closer to the deadline.

Suppose you don’t need the extra speed and capacity that Wi-Fi 7 offers, and you just want something cheap to give you decent coverage throughout your house? Well, that’s where something like the TP-Link Archer AX1450 comes into focus. Walmart has the router on sale this week for $39, a $10 discount off its regular asking price.

The Archer AX1450 is by no means a speed demon, delivering up to 250 Mbps over the 2.4 GHz band and up to 1,201 Mbps on the 5 GHz band. That should be more than sufficient if you have a 1 Gbps or lower broadband connection. You get one GbE WAN port and four GbE LAN ports for connecting your wired devices. The router features four antennas and four wireless streams.

You can manage the Archer AX1450 with the usual webGUI on a desktop/laptop or use the TP-Link Tether app to control the router from your smartphone or tablet.

There’s also the Netgear RAX5, which Walmart has on sale for $44.33 ($35 off its usual selling price). This is another Wi-Fi 6 router delivering up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate speeds. The router covers up to 1,500 square feet and includes a GbE WAN and four GbE LAN ports.

The TP-Link Archer AX1450 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.45 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.

The Netgear RAX5 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.

Keep in mind that the RAX5 isn’t meant for homes that have a ton of smartphones, computers, and smart home devices. It only reliably supports up to 20 wireless devices. So if you have a desktop, a laptop, a couple of TVs, and a couple of smartphones, the RAX5 should do perfectly fine handling the load. If you have more demanding needs, step up to one of the best Wi-Fi 7 routers.

Industry observers note that as I previously mentioned, the TP-Link and Netgear routers are aimed at people who have less demanding wireless needs, and they’re priced to reflect this fact. They won’t win any throughput contests against their newer Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 competition, but those routers will also cost you around twice as much money.

In a recent development, building a modern web API is only half the battle. Ensuring it is secure, resilient, and capable of handling malicious traffic is what separates a hobby project from a production-ready service. When building highly scalable applications, we typically lean on stateless architectures. However, features like token revocation and rate limiting require state.

According to recent reports, in this guide, we will explore the architectural concepts behind building a secure API using FastAPI, Redis, JSON Web Tokens (JWT), and SlowAPI. We will break down the theory, the tech stack, and the flow of data—without getting bogged down in the code.

Before diving into the architecture, it is crucial to understand the role each tool plays in our security model:.

Industry observers note that security starts with how you manage your secrets. The first step in our architectural journey is setting up a configuration file and a local environment file.

Sources indicate that hardcoding secret keys, database URLs, or algorithm types directly into your application is a severe security risk. Instead, we load these from environment variables. The application uses a settings manager to read variables like the Redis host, port, the JWT secret key, the algorithm (typically HS256), and the token expiration time. This ensures that sensitive data stays out of your version control system.

To handle rate limiting and token tracking, we need a connection to Redis. Because FastAPI is inherently asynchronous, we initialize an asynchronous Redis client.

Recent findings suggest that redis acts as the central state-holder for our API. By using Redis, we ensure that even if our API is running on five different servers behind a load balancer, the rate limits and the token blacklists remain globally synchronized.

Recent findings suggest that next, we establish the utility functions that handle the cryptographic heavy lifting. This step is divided into two main parts:.

Here, we initialize the FastAPI application and attach slowapi.

slowapi needs a way to identify the client making the request. By default, it uses the client's IP address. We attach the limiter to the application state and register an exception handler. This ensures that if a user breaches the rate limit, the API gracefully returns a "429 Too Many Requests" error instead of crashing.

We also set up a dependency that acts as a security guard for our protected routes. This dependency intercepts incoming requests, extracts the token, and decodes it. It then checks Redis to see if the token has been blacklisted (for example, if the user logged out before the token expired). If the token is valid and not blacklisted, the request proceeds; otherwise, a "401 Unauthorized" error is thrown.

The login endpoint is where the magic happens. When a user submits their credentials, the API verifies the username and password. In a production scenario, this involves querying a database; in our example, we verify it against a hardcoded credential.

According to recent reports, once the credentials are validated, the API generates a JWT. To ensure we can invalidate this token later if needed, we store the token in Redis with a time-to-live (TTL) that matches the token's expiration time. Finally, the token is returned to the client, which will store it and send it in the Authorization header of future requests.

Finally, we create a route that requires both authentication and rate limiting.

Before the route's logic even executes, two things happen:.

If the client passes both security checks, they are granted access to the highly secure data provided by the route.

In a recent development, to validate this system, you would conceptually walk through several test scenarios. First, you test the login flow with correct and incorrect credentials to ensure tokens are only issued to valid users.

Next, you test the rate limit by rapidly firing requests at the protected route to ensure the "429 Too Many Requests" response triggers. Finally, you test the security guard by trying to access the route with no token, an expired token, and a manually blacklisted token to ensure the API correctly denies access in all scenarios.

Building a secure API requires layering defenses. By combining FastAPI's speed, Redis's fast state management, JWT's stateless authentication, and slowapi's rate-limiting capabilities, you create a system that is both robust and scalable.

While this foundational text explains the core concepts, moving to production requires adding token refresh flows, implementing per-user rate limiting (rather than just IP-based), deploying Redis with high availability, and ensuring your secrets are managed by a secure vault. These practices will ensure your API remains secure as your user base grows.

Industry observers note that OLED panels are quickly becoming a must-have item for desktop PCs. Most of us were introduced to the panel technology in smartphones, and it’s become increasingly popular on laptops. For desktop gamers seeking an immediate visual upgrade, OLED is the way to go, and fortunately, Prime Day is proving to be a great time to take the plunge. From massive DQHD panels on the Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G93SC) to more value-oriented offerings like the Acer Nitro VG277U Xbiip, we have you covered.

Here are the best OLED gaming monitors that we’ve seen so far:.

Mega-ultrawide gaming monitors are not for the faint of heart. Not only can these monitors be quite expensive, but they can also occupy a substantial amount of desktop space. However, for those who have the need (and the space), there are options such as the Samsung 49" Odyssey OLED G9 (G91SD), which is currently on sale for just $799.99 at Amazon.

Recent findings suggest that it features a gorgeous 49-inch QD-OLED panel with a 5120 x 1440 resolution, but instead of a maximum 240 Hz refresh rate, you'll top out at 144 Hz. Brightness tops out at 250 nits (typical), and you'll still get a fast 0.03 ms GtG response time. The monitor supports AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and it's also Nvidia G-Sync compatible. As for ports, you'll find one DisplayPort 1.4, two HDMI 2.1, and two downstream USB-C ports.

The Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G91SD) is a slightly less ambitious 49-inch QD-OLED gaming monitor with a DQHD resolution. Instead of a 240 Hz top speed, the G91SD dials it back to a maximum of 144 Hz.

The AOC Agon Pro AG346UCD is a highly desirable QD-OLED monitor that strikes a sweet spot with its 34-inch WQHD panel and a 165 Hz refresh rate.

If you're looking for something more in a “mid-range” size class, the AOC Agon Pro AG346UCD should be on your shopping list. This is a 34-inch QD-OLED monitor with a 3440 x 1440 resolution and a 165 Hz refresh rate. While that figure may not be as high as the 240 Hz more commonly found with 34-inch panels, the Agon Pro AG346UCD is priced at just $599, taking $50 off its typical asking price. In our review, we praised the monitor for its well-saturated color, excellent contrast, and out-of-the-box accuracy.

The Samsung Odyssey OLED G50SF is a 27-inch 1440p QD-OLED gaming monitor that offers up to 180 Hz refresh rate, 99% coverage of DCI-P3, 0.03ms of response time, and a bunch of features to prevent OLED burn-in.

The Asus ROG Strix XG27ACDNG might be small in stature, but its 27-inch QHD panel delivers a sizzling 360 Hz maximum refresh rate.

One of the best things to happen to gaming monitors in recent years has been the emergence of OLED panel technology. OLED panels are fast, offer rich color and blacker blacks, but have come with a substantial price premium. But as the technology has matured, prices have come down. That fact is exemplified by the 27-inch Samsung Odyssey OLED G50SF, which is right now priced at $319.99.

The Odyssey OLED G50SF features a QD-OLED panel measuring 27 inches with a QHD resolution of 2560×1440, which is currently the sweet spot for PC gaming. It supports up to a 180 Hz refresh rate via DisplayPort and 144 Hz through HDMI. Samsung claims that the display offers a response time of 0.03ms (GTG), essentially offering smooth and responsive visuals during fast action. With G-Sync compatibility and support for AMD FreeSync, expect zero screen lag and image tearing.

Another option is the Asus ROG Strix XG27ACDNG, which also sports a 27-inch QHD QD-OLED panel. When the ROG Strix XG27ACDNG arrived in our testing lab, we noted its accuracy, fast response, and stunning image quality. The monitor also boasts a 360 Hz refresh rate for ultra-twitch gamers. At the moment, the ROG Strix XG27ACDNG is on sale for $549, representing a 28% savings.

#139619. Grand Theft Auto 6 launch day - all the news and rection as GTA 6 arrived around the world

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3456 w)
📖 Baca

Grand Theft Auto 6 launch day - all the news and rection as GTA 6 arrived around the world

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3456 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide.
  • Sources indicate that have you played it yet?
  • More broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide. It's destined to become the largest video game release of all time, and probably one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time. So we're doing a launch day live blog to chart its arrival in the world.

Sources indicate that have you played it yet? I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go. I couldn't manage it but my college-age son was contemplating it. And if you have played it, what do you think - what are your early impressions? Is this what you were waiting for?

More broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world. I've already seen nearly all mainstream news and media outlets attempt to cover the game - and many other kinds of businesses - so will GTA 6 make people reappraise video games?

In a recent development, moreover, exactly how big will the launch be? The record books are ready to be written in, but what exactly will be written? And how will other games fare in GTA's wake - better, or worse? There's lots to consider as the ripples spread around the world.

In a recent development, we'll pull-in stories and developments, and your comments, as we chart the arrival of Rockstar's game around the world. Let's get to it.

Our live coverage of this event has finished.

Industry observers note that an historic day in gaming and there's loads to unpack. But to begin with, this: did you take a day off to play GTA 6, and have you played it yet?

Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

Industry observers note that the marketing push by Rockstar to have GTA 6 imprint on real-world cities has been impressive to see. There have been festivals in Miami, Selfridges dedicated a portion of its department store to selling GTA merch, but there's more than this besides. The London Standard summarised much of the activity in London in a video on Instagram.

A post shared by The Standard (@thelondonstandard).

Rockstar employment tribunal verdict could take weeks.

Industry observers note that the din of release is in danger of drowning out the Rockstar employment tribunal that came to a close this week in Scotland. Former Eurogamer video producer Chris Bratt - now co-owner of People Make Games - has been following the case closely, and reported yesterday that a verdict in the case could take "weeks".

According to recent reports, he quotes Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Sources indicate that and that's it for the Rockstar tribunal! We await the judge's decision, but how long will it take? Judge Lucy Wiseman: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Yesterday, we independently confirmed that most, if not all, of the fired Rockstar employees are credited in the GTA 6 credits - which are, according to Chris Tapsell, our reviewer, an enormous thing in their own right.

Here’s how massive it is, news-wise:.

Yesterday, my mother _(whose single dabble in gaming over the years can be described as,“working out the way to bypass the Brontosaurus Guarding Causeway in the text adventure Time Machine, is to GIVE it the Ship’s Biscuit found aboard the Marie Celeste”)_ texted me to ask if I was “ready for tomorrow?”.

I instantly assumed I’d made or hinted at some plan to do something with her and subsequently forgotten.

Sources indicate that BUT, NO. She was asking if I was ready for GTA. A product I have never mentioned in her presence in all my many years.

So if you’ve got the over-seventies non-gamers talking… I’d say you’ve cracked it.

In a recent development, goodness! And will your mother also be playing it?

My inbox is flooded with all kinds of brands trying to get in on the GTA 6 hype.

The most recent one? Petrol prices. "Having to refuel your car in GTA 6 adds another layer of realism to the game, but it's something real-life drivers have to think about every time they get behind the wheel," noted Beth Fountain, fuel expert at somewhere called Interfuels.

"With petrol and diesel prices remaining high, filling up can take a significant chunk out of someone's monthly budget, particularly for those who rely on their vehicles for work or regular travel.

"While players might find the new mechanic frustrating, it's a reminder of how much we depend on fuel in everyday life and how rapidly those costs can add up.".

There's another one from Just Eat, the food delivery company, which has apparently made a real controller with Just Eat order button on it for you to order food while gaming. It's not specifically GTA 6-linked but it's jumping on that bandwagon. The controller is apparently synced to your Just Eat account. Imagine mashing that by accident and having an accidental feast turn up.

"When you're deep into a high-stakes gaming session nothing kills the moment faster than having to pause the action just to sort out food. With the Just ChEAT Button, Just Eat has unlocked the ultimate hack to evade the kitchen, enabling gamers to stay just where they are and locked into play," said Just East UK and Ireland marketing director Tina Koehler.

According to recent reports, it's not clear where you can buy this controller or how much it costs. It's described as "limited edition". I wonder if that means only one has been made.

The goofy things people are already doing in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that many people are playing GTA 6 already of course and doing expectedly bizarre things in it. From lobbing hammers like Crocodile Dundee lobs cans of tinned food, to dropkicking people, to attempting to dive through a car window while oiled up and in one's pants - Connor has rounded up some of the goofiest clips around.

You are brilliant, Eurogamer readers!

I just want to resurface the winning entry to the GTA memories competition we ran at the tail-end of last week, because it's funny and uplifting, and I still smile about it.

My favourite GTA memory is introducing my nan to Vice City.

She'd never played a video game before, so I told her she could pretty much do whatever she wanted.

She spent the first 20 minutes driving around obeying traffic lights and apologising whenever she bumped into another car.

Then she accidentally punched someone.

I don't know what happened, but something just clicked.

Within half an hour she'd stolen a police car, run over several pedestrians and was shouting at the telly because the police wouldn’t leave her alone.

My grandad came in to see what all the noise was about.

According to recent reports, without even looking up she just noted, "I'm wanted for murder, Barry. Put the kettle on.".

Genuinely one of the funniest afternoons of my childhood.

In a recent development, I'm on the management team for a charity and they've scheduled their AGM for tonight at 6pm. Of all the dates! I've had to weigh up not doing my duty for selfish video game reasons.

I must be growing up because I've decided that going to the AGM is the right thing to do and that GTA 6 probably isn't that good, anyway. Right?

Well! Allow the Eurogamer comments to decide. I think you should set GTA 6 up in another room in the building you're holding the AGM in, and find excuses during it to nip out and play. It'll be like a Mrs Doubtfire moment. Nothing can go wrong.

In a recent development, another email from a shopping comparison site, Idealo, and this time about PS5 Pro demand, which has apparently leapt by 57 percent week on week because of GTA 6. This, by the way, is exactly what the industry was hoping would happen - that GTA 6 would reinvigorate console sales, which were slumping, not least because of their unprecedented rising prices. Apparently the price of PS5 consoles is rising in step with this demand.

"Grand Theft Auto launches are major cultural moments, and GTA 6 is already having a noticeable impact on the wider gaming market, particularly when it comes to console demand," Katy Phillips from Idealo remarked.

"We're seeing a significant increase in interest in the PS5 Pro, with demand jumping by 57 percent in the week leading up to launch. At the same time, the price of the console has climbed by more than £450 since the end of October.".

GTA 6 videos you might find helpful.

In a recent development, IGN has produced a bunch of good Grand Theft Auto 6 videos I'm surfacing here in case you've missed them. There are a few performance-related videos of the game running on PlayStation and Xbox hardware:.

There's also footage of the first 15 minutes of the first mission:.

And some scuba diving and treasure hunting:.

GTA 6 is Metacritic's highest rated game ever.

Recent findings suggest that A notable moment yesterday was GTA 6 being crowned as the highest-rated game ever on review-averaging site Metacritic. The game currently holds a 99 score there, averaged from 156 critics' reviews. The previous champion was the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, from 1998, with the same 99 average critics score. Will it retain the title as the days and weeks unfold?

Chris' expansive GTA 6 review is of course one of those contributing to that score. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

More ridiculous GTA 6 launch piggybacking and this time it's an email with a therapist talking about how the game might help teens with their dating outlooks.

Says Natalie Buchwald, therapist and founder of Manhattan Mental Health Counseling:.

"Psychologists sometimes talk about 'relationship scripts': the unspoken expectations we absorb about how relationships work, what partners owe each other and what success looks like. We pick these up long before we have much experience of our own, from family, friends, online spaces and the stories we see in entertainment.

It has been revealed that "No single film, game or influencer shapes someone's values on its own. What matters more is the overall mix of messages a person encounters, and whether they have the space to question them. That's particularly relevant now that dating advice is so widely available online, where some content frames relationships around status, control or getting something in return, rather than mutual respect.

According to recent reports, "That's why the most useful thing parents can do isn't to hand over a set of rules. It's to help young people think critically about the scripts they're picking up. Being curious rather than critical, and asking what they've seen, what they think of it and what they believe makes a good partner, tends to keep conversations open.

According to recent reports, "Entertainment can play a helpful role here. A story built around a partnership, like Jason and Lucia's, can give parents a natural, low pressure starting point for conversations that might otherwise feel awkward.".

Industry observers note that chris referenced some of this in his review, praising Jason's tender and caring side, and his not being a toxic asshole. GTA 6 is also the first game to not only feature a couple but a female playable lead, having very much revolved around male fantasies in the past.

You can't use cheat in GTA 6 until you finish the main story.

A reminder that cheats aren't usable in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you've finished the main story. Chris confirmed this yesterday, and offered details about cheats do work in the game when you've unlocked them.

More brand opportunism, this time optician Specsavers, and at least this one has a novel approach: a spoof partnership with a GTA company that has nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto.

Specsavers is circulating a very budget-looking partnership with a trucking company called GTA Transport. It's billed as a "mix-up" in an email, but it's all far too staged and knowing to really be one.

According to recent reports, "It might not be the GTA partnership I originally had in mind but a deal's a deal," said Specsavers marketing person Neil Liddle. "I'm pleased to offer every driver at GTA Transport a free eye test.".

Sources indicate that bugz Singh at GTA Transport stated: "We were surprised when Specsavers got in touch, but we're delighted to be the GTA they've teamed up with. Our drivers spend all day on the road, so they're looking forward to their eye tests.".

The visuals are just something else. Even at this early stage, the story has already got me interested and invested in Jason and Lucia. And to top it all off, when I first started messing around with the car radio, ‘Master of Puppets’ was playing.

It has been revealed that the second thing is that like all gtas is serves a reminder of what a hellscape urban America is. I’ve never been to the keys, but what looks like it should be a lovely set of islands is of course mostly a massive highway.

In a recent development, ...long story short, what was intended to be a 1 hour go on a school night ended up being 3 hours and I slept through my alarm and am working from home today! I'll be playing this and pretty much only this for the next month or 2, no doubt...haven't been gripped by a game since Clair Obscure...nice to have that feeling back!

Some nice accounts of playing the game so far. Keep 'em coming!

GTA 6 developers fear for their jobs now the game has shipped.

In a recent development, rockstar and Take-Two stand to make billions of dollars from GTA 6, but there's an enormous workforce - 4,711 people at last count - working at the GTA studio. Will they keep their jobs now the game has come out? That staff-count more than doubled after Red Dead Redemption 2 was released but will it grow again now?

Industry observers note that fears of lay-offs reach top volume both as the game is released and as Rockstar workers vote wheter to formally recognise a workers union there - a union that's proved so problematic in the past. Sherif has the full story below.

GameStop boss slams 'code in a box' trend in wake of GTA 6's discless release.

The boss of game-related retailer GameStop has spoken out about the trend of 'code in a box' game releases. This, of course, is pertinent this week with the discless release of GTA 6.

"When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," GameStop boss Ryan Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." Dom has the full story:.

In a recent development, I have always wondered if one of the reasons I bounced off 5 was that I got it a long while down the line. (Also... I really didn't like the main characters).

Decided to be part of this "global media event" and bought it last night.

The intro is pretty gripping story wise, with a decent twist that somehow was kept completely under wraps.

Recent findings suggest that driving takes some getting used to, but the use of adaptive triggers on PS5 is great for this making cruising fairly easy. The traffic density and “smaller” roads really make getting about the city nicely realistically annoying. Spending more time cruising than normal for a GTA.

Being quoted is the risk one runs!

The spoof websites aren't in GTA 6 because Rockstar didn't think they were "necessary".

Sources indicate that the spoof websites of previous GTA games don't make it into GTA 6. Apparently Rockstar didn't deem them "necessary". Let me tell you, as someone who writes for a website, that cuts deep.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector has strong words for Rockstar about GTA 6.

According to recent reports, deus Ex legend Warren Spector, who was also involved in the making of influential series like Thief, System Shock and Ultima Underworld, has a few strong words to say about GTA 6. Or rather not GTA 6 itself but the colossal workforce, budget and development time Rockstar had to make i with.

"A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries," Spector noted. "Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

I'm genuinely surprised that some gaming companies are ernestly trying to release and market their games today of all days - even this week. Did you want to know about a Goat Simulator 3 expansion that arrived today, called Dizzyworld? Well, now you do. And it's by far the only game I'm being sent press releases about.

My favourite press release about a game unrelated to GTA 6 - though it sounds like a parody that could be in the game - is one that made me do a double-take. "Sperm Adventure 'Become' Delayed to First Half of 2027," it read. The entire press release is packed with innuendo. And it's - judging by its Steam page - a real thing. Will you "embark on life's greatest tiny journey"?

GTA 6 is dominating Twitch viewer figures in a massive way.

Back to GTA 6, and the impact of this game's arrival can be seen clearly on Twitch viewership numbers at the moment. GTA 6 is by far the most watched category on the streaming platform, with more than 1.6 million viewers. The next highest category is the broad "just chatting" category 2ith 330k viewers, followed by World of Warcraft with 72k viewers.

For balance, presentation and intro to story/characters are great.

"Laser Disc vibes" is not a phrase I've heard before, but I like it and think I'll steal it.

All 34 of the fired Rockstar employees are in the GTA 6 credits.

Here's a curious development. With Rockstar publishing the full cast list for GTA 6, I've been more able to cross-check the names of the 34 fired employees against it. And, success, they do all appear in the credits. But six of them are not contained in the "former employees" section of the credits, where everyone else is, which is curious. I'm trying to find out what gives.

Jason Duval actor finally confirmed.

Sources indicate that incidentally, that full cast list also confirms - finally - who the actor is that plays Jason Duval in the game. And, yes, it's Dylan Rourke, who everyone thought it was.

More than 2 million people used Fresh Zealand trick to play GTA 6 early.

Recent findings suggest that I tried doing the New Zealand trick on my PS5 yesterday evening - I'd spent the entire afternoon convinced it would be a doddle to play GTA 6 early doing so. It wasn't. So I played Galactic Racers instead (which is great).

Nevertheless, millions of people did use the Upcoming Zealand time-zone trick to play the game early - more than 2 million people, in fact, which is more than a third of the population of the country.

You can make GTA 6 easier by altering two important settings.

As people start playing the game, issues of difficulty come up, and altering the game to your preference. And as Dom reported, there are two very important changes you can make to the game - in lieu of difficulty settings - to change how challenging it is to play.

How are you all doing? It's nearly the end of the day - are you excited about getting home to play the game? Are you nonplussed? Are you perhaps playing the game already? Temperature check! As they say.

Recent findings suggest that the UK working day is coming to an end here. Thanks everyone for popping in and good luck exploring the game tonight, if you are. That's a wrap on our rolling coverage for today, though our general news coverage continues into the evening.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

1. Cheapest DDR52. Cheapest DDR4.

In today's market, memory has become one of the most critical and expensive components in any build, and prices have only worsened thanks to the ongoing global DRAM shortage. We're keeping an eye on the volatile memory pricing to help identify any good deals that may arise.

Recent findings suggest that now, even more so than before the shortage began, price tags are fluctuating significantly from day to day, and it's becoming increasingly complex to tell when you're getting a fair deal versus overpaying for the same memory kit. We've compiled this comprehensive RAM price tracker that monitors the availability and pricing of different DDR5 and DDR4 memory kits across major U.S. retailers. Our goal is to take the guesswork out of memory shopping and help you make an informed purchasing decision.

We update this index regularly with the lowest prices available in the U.S. market for each memory kit. Our tracker covers a range of capacities and speeds across both budget and premium brands. We list the lowest price for each available memory kit, regardless of manufacturer, so you see the absolute best deals currently on offer.

It has been revealed that the general availability of many memory kits is limited, with truly exceptional deals scarce and often selling out within seconds of appearing. High-capacity kits, particularly DDR5, frequently show the most severe stock shortages and price premiums. Therefore, timing and vigilance are especially crucial when shopping for memory in current times. Whether you're budget-conscious and want the best bang for your buck, or you're building a premium system and want the best RAM for gaming available, our index further below gives you the data you need to make the right purchase.

You can also check out our list of the best RAM and our RAM benchmark hierarchy to see evergreen performance data to help you make an informed decision when choosing a new GPU for your system.

Here are a few exceptional Black Friday RAM deals, but below that, we have a full list of all the lowest-priced RAM on the market.

Recent findings suggest that get a great deal on standalone RAM from Newegg. This deal is currently the lowest priced DDR5-6000 available. The T-Force Delta RGB not only adds flair to your chassis, but does so with decent speeds.

According to recent reports, this RGB-laden kit from Corsair sports a CAS latency of 36 and is tested at 1.35 volts. This pair of 16GB memory sticks is colored black on the aluminum heat spreader, with RGB lighting running along the spine.

Above are a few of the standout deals from the Black Friday event, which is at the moment taking place. For a more extensive list of Black Friday deals, head to our Black Friday RAM deals article.

According to recent reports, DDR5 memory prices have exploded over the last year, with triple and, in some cases, quadruple increases. For instance, a conventional 32GB (2x16GB) DDR5-6000 memory kit sold for around $100 to $200 in October 2025, but the same kit now starts at $430, if it's even in stock.

Retailers are taking advantage of the DRAM shortage, just as they did with the graphics card shortage a few years ago. They've started raising DDR5 prices to align with current market conditions and sometimes bundle DDR5 memory kits with processor or motherboard purchases.

Industry observers note that nonetheless, these DDR5 memory kits sometimes sell for more reasonable prices. However, you have to be quick to pull the trigger, as scalpers and automated shopping bots tend to gobble up what little stock is left.

Sources indicate that the rising prices of DDR5 memory kits have forced some consumers to stick with DDR4. However, DDR4 has also seen price hikes over the last three months, though not as drastic as DDR5. We've seen the pricing double to triple.

According to recent reports, for reference, it was common to find 32GB (2x16GB) DDR4 memory kits selling for between $60 to $90 back in October 2025. Jump to January 2026, and the same memory kit could cost anywhere between $150 and $180, so DDR4 isn't exactly a safe haven for consumers.

Industry observers note that we've seen more reasonably priced DDR4 memory kits on the market than DDR5. Logically, it makes little sense to build a DDR4-based system now due to processor and motherboard availability. However, if you're in desperate need of a DDR4 memory upgrade, there are viable options on the market.

CFTC and Justice Department sue Arkansas and Louisiana over event-contract crackdowns

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In two days, federal authorities filed suits against two states that treat prediction markets as illegal gambling.
  • The federal government has opened two newly introduced court fights with states over prediction markets.
  • Industry observers note that the Arkansas complaint carries case number 4:26-cv-01255-BSM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In two days, federal authorities filed suits against two states that treat prediction markets as illegal gambling. The cases could decide whether state gaming regulators or the CFTC control sports event contracts, which compete with licensed sportsbooks and online casinos.

The federal government has opened two newly introduced court fights with states over prediction markets. Both target state actions against event contracts offered on CFTC-regulated exchanges. Arkansas and Louisiana treat those contracts as illegal gambling. Washington argues that federal law takes priority.

Industry observers note that the Arkansas complaint carries case number 4:26-cv-01255-BSM. It is aimed at the enforcement action Griffin filed against KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc. That state suit alleges multiple violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. It seeks restitution, penalties, taxes and injunctive relief.

In release 9325-26, the CFTC mentioned Arkansas could seek civil penalties against CFTC-registered exchanges that could reach hundreds of millions of dollars. The federal suit also aims to stop the state from halting event-contract trading. The government wants a preliminary and permanent injunction. That order would bar Arkansas officials from investigating CFTC-regulated entities, their affiliates and partners. It would also stop them from enforcing state law against those firms over transactions on designated contract markets.

Griffin’s stance is not latest. In October 2025, he issued a formal opinion that sports event contracts are gambling and require a license. The new case brings the preemption fight into the Eighth Circuit, which has not yet ruled on the question.

With Arkansas added, the CFTC’s tally of state lawsuits over federal authority reaches 11. The agency has also filed amicus briefs in four federal appeals courts and one state supreme court.

The Louisiana case moved within a day. Judge Jeffrey Johnson of the 21st Judicial District Court in Tangipahoa Parish signed the restraining order. The named entities are linked to Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, Crypto.com, Coinbase, Gemini, ForecastEx, Novig, Underdog, IG Group and ProphetX.

Industry observers note that in release 9326-26, the CFTC said the order shut down more than 30 companies tied to CFTC-regulated derivatives without giving them notice or a chance to be heard. The federal suit was filed in the Eastern District of Louisiana. It names the state, Attorney General Liz Murrill, the Louisiana Gaming Control Board and the state police gaming enforcement division. It asks the court to declare state gambling laws preempted. It also seeks to stop Louisiana from enforcing or extending the state order.

🚨Breaking: Louisiana judge orders temporary restraining order prohibiting Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Robinhood, and other “prediction market” operators from continuing their unlicensed and unregulated illegal gambling in Louisiana.

It’s not complicated: if you aren’t a… pic.twitter.com/gzrQlN9CCL.

— Attorney General Liz Murrill (@AGLizMurrill) November 12, 2026.

The exchange between officials has been sharp. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig described Louisiana’s emergency suit as “naked lawfare and a cynical political stunt.” On Nov. 14, Murrill answered on X. She accused Selig of “flatly false statements” and argued that states have regulated gambling for 250 years.

For licensed sportsbooks and online casinos, the outcome matters directly. If federal preemption holds, sports event contracts could operate outside state gaming rules in both states. The federal requests to block both states’ actions now go before the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern Districts of Arkansas and Louisiana.

#139612. Playing GTA 6 this weekend? Here's 16 spoiler-free tips for your first playthrough

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1794 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Playing GTA 6 this weekend? Here's 16 spoiler-free tips for your first playthrough

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1794 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's launch weekend for GTA 6 - in case you hadn't noticed - and since I've played the best part of a hundred hours of this thing, I thought it might be useful to share a few pieces of advice from my time with it.
  • Many of these are most applicable for the early game, but there are a few that'll be worth bearing in mind throughout.
  • In a recent development, the below list is spoiler-free, so you can relax if you're anxious about going through the story entirely fresh.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's launch weekend for GTA 6 - in case you hadn't noticed - and since I've played the best part of a hundred hours of this thing, I thought it might be useful to share a few pieces of advice from my time with it.

Many of these are most applicable for the early game, but there are a few that'll be worth bearing in mind throughout. After last night's driving around I would also maybe add in a quick bonus one, come to think of it: watch out for cyclists making last-minute left turns. Or don't, actually. Half of this lot deserve it….

In a recent development, the below list is spoiler-free, so you can relax if you're anxious about going through the story entirely fresh. Though naturally I do explain the way some parts of this game work, taking away some of the sense of discovery. You can take my word for it that there's plenty more to discover beyond this though, so worry not.

If you'd like even more help navigating Leonida, then check out our wonderful guide team's GTA 6 walkthrough.

Recent findings suggest that the number one thing I'd tell people to do in GTA 6 is to create lots of save files and, as you progress and start needing to overwrite them, to try to keep a roughly even spread of files through each chapter. There are various reasons for this - for one, while the game autosaves, it doesn't seem to do that successfully if you suddenly lose power to the console or witness a rare game crash, so it'll preserve your progress. More than that: GTA's story and missions are surprisingly, perhaps mysteriously reactive. Quite a lot can differ, and so being able to go back and make different choices, or play the game differently, will be something 'future you' likely appreciates.

In the very early game you won't have access to a bank account, but once you do: you should put every bit of cash you have in there as soon as you can. Cash is lost on death or arrest - which can happen quite often in GTA 6, funnily enough - and there's no real benefit to carrying it around. Just about everything, besides in-game strippers, can be paid for via your BuckMe account directly. And there's a relatively low $20,000 limit you really don't want to hit in the middle of raiding a gang hideout, either.

In a recent development, GTA 6 has a luxurious range of customisation settings, from hiding notifications about your relationship to reinstating the old 'tap to sprint' control scheme. The accessibility settings - while crucially I'm not an expert - seem considerable. And there are somewhat disguised difficult settings here around enemy damage taken and encounters with the police.

Fairly early in the game you'll gain access to the Scooter Bros. App, which lets you repair or summon your owned vehicles at will. Crucially, there's also an option to pay a one-off fee to unlock three free uses of the app per day. At $12,000, in the early game this is a lot of dosh, but once you rack up that kind of money after advancing through the game a little, it's well worth the initial cost. The sooner you unlock it, the more value it provides over time on a cost-per-use basis. And trust me when I say: as the game's intensity ramps up, you will probably find yourself needing to repair and recover your vehicles quite often. (Also, in Chapter 1, before you get access to the app, you can access the same service by going to your phone's contacts and calling Joey - handy!).

Rockstar has somewhat disincentivised it by adding a cost and putting it in your phone's apps rather than the main map screen, but you can fast travel around Leonida if you ever want or need to. This is done via the RideMe Uber-like app. It's not cheap - you'll need to pay both the fee for the journey and an additional $100 to skip that journey and instantly arrive at your destination, but in certain scenarios it might prove useful. To skip the journey, hold L2/LT once in the cab, and then hold down Triangle/Y when the option is shown. However….

In a recent development, while it's possible to journey-skip your way around this world, having tested that first hand I'd advise against it. It might be obvious, but GTA 6 is genuinely designed around you manually travelling around, typically in the car. If you skip all your commutes between missions or locations, you'll miss out on the game's dozens and dozens of emergent events, which lead to anything from one-off jokes to entire mission chains. The car is also, in a way, kind of the heart of the entire game. Relish the intentional slowness!

Again, avoiding spoilers here, but in the mid game the 'true' loop of GTA 6 gameplay will properly reveal itself, in all the many methods of earning money and the increased emphasis on doing so. You can of course play the game however you like, but having reached the end and looked back from that point, I found that if there was a particular moment to set aside as the time for aimlessly exploring the world, it was from around Chapter 3 onwards. You'll have enough tools to be able to see it at more or less its fullest then, but also won't have missed anything essential by waiting until that point to take your foot off the pedal either.

A handy early-game tip here that even I missed when I was playing, but have since discovered: two islands in the small cluster of them to the south-west of Jason's early game home each house a really useful weapon, in a silenced pistol and a handy shotgun. You'll own these permanently once found, and so they can be incredibly helpful for navigating missions with maximum or minimal violence. Look for shipwrecks on those islands to find them. The pistol is hidden under a little hatch on the deck of a shipwreck on the southernmost point of the south-easternmost island. The shotgun is next to a small wooden wrecked boat around the middle of the northernmost island.

Industry observers note that A mechanic I slightly underused at first was the ability to 'save' a given outfit to your car. You can do this either from your car's trunk or from the wardrobe, and it's hugely useful as you start to get into more elaborate scrapes with the police (and also if you just like to role-play a bit and don the right outfit for the right occasion).

Sources indicate that there are lots of reasons for this, from the moments of intimacy it affords you with your partner, to the extra buffs you can get from resting. Sleep at home, for instance, and you can then immediately pet your snake (ahem), down a coffee or drink from the fridge, grab an apple and take a shower for a range of buffs across health, stamina, and focus. Each of these will last quite some time, so it's worth the few minutes of time to do them. Eating and drinking regularly also helps you maximise gains in the gym.

Rockstar seems to enjoy the concept of a game within a game, and that's exemplified well by the in-game phone. You can find missions via scrolling Snapmatic, it's in-game social media, or from texting various contacts you pick up as the game progresses. It's worth checking it every now and then just to see if anything interesting - or just funny or absurd - might pop up.

Car trunks, both those belonging to the public and the police, are often well worth a look. Even if you're promptly nabbing a car for a short-term dash, take a moment to check the boot for anything worthwhile. We've found everything from sellable narcotics to very useful weapons in there. In cop cars, that goes up several notches, too.

Sources indicate that A small thing, but in-mission checkpoints are relatively generous in GTA 6. If you really wanted to complete a mission a certain way - undetected or non-violent, say - then don't be afraid to quickly re-load rather than feeling you need to manually load up an earlier save, or give up on your goal entirely. It's also helped me out with a few minor progress-jamming bugs along the way too.

Recent findings suggest that this might seem obvious, but it's worth emphasising for early-game players: it's very, very rare that you actually need to kill anybody in GTA 6. Enemies are fully incapacitated when you see a yellow hit marker over your crosshairs, even if that just comes from blasting away at their toes. If you make a habit of navigating combat this way then that also makes it much easier to recover your 'Professional' criminal status if you ever do decide to go full rampage. Though you can, of course, ultimately play this game however you like. Just be aware there may be consequences, known and unknown, as you go. Also: don't forget to click the right analog stick to aim down sights - it's an easy thing to forget when playing a third-person shooter like this, and not always the best way to operate, but incredibly helpful in select circumstances.

Throughout the game you'll have a 'family savings' goal to hit. As you progress you'll find more ways to earn money much faster, and so it's easy to make up for lost time here if, later on, you decide that actually you do want to think about the future after all. But that grind will be a fair bit less painful if you chip away at the target as you go. As long as you save yourself some fun money - a few hundred in the early game, few thousand in the mid game, and a few tens of thousands late on - then you'll have enough to do key things like buying new garages to register vehicles, or paying to register them themselves.

According to recent reports, throughout your time with GTA 6 you'll encounter moments when you need to make a choice. Interestingly, I noticed at least a few occasions where a scenario changed when I just waited, doing nothing at all. Sometimes that might mean a choice is made for you - so waiting is a risk - but on other occasions new options become available. Sometimes they might mean a genuinely different consequence, others they might just lead to characters reacting in a certain kind of way. But it's worth experimenting - your first options aren't always your only ones.

It has been revealed that the Creative Labs Pebble V2 speakers are a go-to recommendation for cheap PC speakers here at Tom's Hardware, and for good reason. As you can read about in our review of the larger Creative Pebble Pro speakers, this range offers plenty of headroom, providing clean sound at higher volumes despite the tiny woofer size (just two inches). Like many Bluetooth speakers, the Pebble V2 set features passive radiators, capturing low-end frequencies to give the impression of a subwoofer. Of course, it's not the same as a subwoofer, but passive bass chambers help a lot with these smaller speakers.

It has been revealed that you connect the speakers over a 3.5mm cable for audio, and power them with USB-C (the speakers call for a 10W port). Sustained RMS power is just 8W for the speakers, but they can peak a bit higher at 16W. They run lower by default, but a high-gain switch on the back will kick the power amp into full gear if you need the speakers louder.

The G2000 speakers from Edifier come with a peak power raing of 32W and a frequency response of 98 Hz up to 22 kHz, along with analog and Bluetooth connections.

In a recent development, the Edifer G2000 speakers double the power output of the Pebble V2's, and they feature larger 2.75-inch drivers (though no tweeter). At $80 on sale, they're much more expensive, but Edifier justifies the extra price with USB and Bluetooth output, alongside a standard 3.5mm connection, as well as a dedicated power adapter to avoid unwanted noise over USB power. If you want to expand your setup, there's also a subwoofer output.

RMS power here is 16W, giving you significantly more headroom at higher volumes to avoid any distortion. The 2.75-inch full range drivers offers decent low-end, though the frequency response cuts off just below 100 Hz, leaving precious sub-region frequencies out of the sonic picture. That gives you a good cutoff point to add a subwoofer, however.

The Edifier M60 speakers feature a 3-inch woofer and 1-inch tweeter, as well as 66W of total output across the four drivers.

Edifer's M60 speakers are larger, and they take some obvious notes from Audioengine. They're not quite the same as the A2+ speakers, however. The M60s feature a 3-inch woofer and 1-inch tweeter, with an average RMS of 66W across all four drivers (18W each for the woofers, and 15W for the tweeters).

In a recent development, the speakers come with a Hi-Res audio certification, extending the frequency response up from the typical 20 kHz to 40 kHz. Although the human ear typically can't hear about 20 kHz, extra harmonic information down in the audible range of frequencies can add richness to the sound. The speakers can output via USB-C, Bluetooth 5.3, or a 3.5mm, and they come with included stands, which is something even AudioEngine lacks.

These 6.81 x 4.68 x 5.51-inch speakers have attractive removable cloth fronts, 10-degree angled stands to aim them up at your ears, and they performed well in our testing. They also have ample connectivity, with Bluetooth 5.3 LE, USB-C, RCA (with a built-in Phono stage for vinyl record players), optical, and a subwoofer connector.

Recent findings suggest that for slightly more than the M60s, we have a pair of the GX-10DB speakers from the Japanese brand Onkyo. They come with 3-inch woofers, as well, though slightly smaller 0.75-inch tweets, as well as a Class D amp that can drive RMS of 30W through the speakers. Onkyo gives you a ton of ways to connect to the speakers, including USB-C, optical, Bluetooth, and RCA. The RCA inputs feature a phono stage for use with a turntable, as well.

Although these are relatively inexpensive speakers, Onkyo still makes them feel premium with removable speaker grilles and built-in, wood-finished stands that angle the speakers up toward your ears.

This desktop speaker includes dual four-inch drivers, as well as an integrated EQ and wireless remote.

If bookshelf speakers aren't your speed, you can save 44% on the Edifier D12 all-in-one desktop speaker. It's a 70-watt speaker with Bluetooth, RCA, and 3.5mm inputs with an attractive wood-grain finish and sleek removeable front grille that sports the Edifier logo.

The speaker is equipped with dual 4-inch drivers along with two 19mm silk down tweeters. Two bass radiator ports provide low-end support. At the top of the speaker, you'll find bass, middle, and treble controls, and the speaker includes a remote so you can control it wirelessly.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for maximum power, you get 120W of goodness with Edifier's S1000MKII speakers, which are on sale for $100 off right now. These are large speakers with 5.5-inch aluminum alloy drivers and 1-inch titanium dome tweeters.

It features Bluetooth, optical, coaxial, and RCA inputs, and there's a universal bass and treble control. These are large bookshelf speakers meant for listening to music, so make sure you have a large-enough desk to fit them byside your monitor.

#139608. I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1293 w)
